episodes.210699: A cold front slowly dropping in from the north triggered scattered to numerous showers and thunderstorms in an unseasonably warm airmass. A few of the storms produced gale-force wind gusts over the waters, both during the afternoon and with a second wave in the evening.
episodes.210700: A cold front slowly dropping in from the north triggered scattered to numerous showers and thunderstorms in an unseasonably warm airmass. A few of the storms produced sporadic damaging wind gusts and large hail, both during the afternoon and with a second wave in the evening.
episodes.210813: On April 2nd's early evening, an upper level short wave disturbance crossing the Middle Mississppi Valley, and associated 1000-mb surface low pressure tracking quickly from Iowa to Wiscomsin, placed central Indiana within its warm sector.  The conditional set-up for severe weather included steep 0-3 km lapse rates, and corresponding DCAPE values of 500-800 J/kg extending along and just east of the Wabash Valley.  A resultant quasi-linear convective system (QLCS) crossed western central Indiana, producing widely scattered damaging straight line winds.  The system's overall high cloud base mitigated any tornado production except where a brief EF-0 was spawned in Parke County.
episodes.211067: The first of April saw the third consecutive day of severe thunderstorms across the region. An upper level storm system moving out of the Rockies into the Central Plains brought moisture and lift over West Texas creating widespread rain showers and thunderstorms. Surface conditions across the caprock were relatively dry which led to numerous virga showers that brought severe wind gusts. Once this activity reached better moisture off the caprock, the showers developed into severe thunderstorms producing severe wind gusts. ||High wind gusts (non-thunderstorms) from Texas Tech University West Texas mesonet sites are listed below:||67 mph at New Deal (Lubbock County),|64 mph at Shallowater (Lubbock County),|62 mph at Reese Center (Lubbock County), |58 mph at Floydada (Floyd County), and|58 mph at Olton (Lamb County).||High wind reports (non-thunderstorms) from Automated Surface Observing Systems (ASOS) are listed below:||64 mph at Lubbock International Airport (Lubbock County).
episodes.211289: A dryline set up over central portions of the Permian Basin, extending southward towards the Big Bend. A nearby shortwave encouraged thunderstorm development east of this dryline. A couple of thunderstorms produced severe winds in the Permian Basin. Meanwhile, strong winds aloft coupled with the passage of a Pacific front allowed for high winds in the Guadalupe Mountains and in far northern portions of Lea County in SE New Mexico.
episodes.211295: Several rounds of strong to severe thunderstorms pressed through West Virginia on April 1st as a cold front progressed overhead. The first notable storm kicked things off shortly after midday in Wayne County, with large hail and damaging wind gusts that resulted in local power outages. Additional storm damage progressed through the state over the course of the afternoon and evening as more development occurred ahead of the frontal passage. In addition to the downed trees and power lines, heavy downpours accompanying storms in the Parkersburg area led to street flooding along several roads in the city. The loss of daytime heating brought the severe threat of storms to an end that evening.
episodes.211371: Scattered thunderstorms moved across portions of northern Illinois during the evening of April 2nd producing wind damage and three tornadoes.
episodes.211639: A quasi-stationary front drifted into northern Virginia, supported aloft by a weak upper level trough, provided instability for a few severe thunderstorms to develop. Lapse rates of around 6-7 degrees C/km and CAPE values between 1000-2000 J/kg were observed, in addition to afternoon surface temperatures in the 80s, triggered thunderstorms that produced large hail along the Blue Ridge into the Piedmont.
episodes.211679: Stronger storms occurred over Lee county and later moved over Somerville.
episodes.211761: An intensifying upper storm system instigated a period of severe thunderstorms across much of the WFO Norman Forecast area during the evening of the 1st. Storm development occurred both along a quasi-stationary boundary across northern Oklahoma and along an accelerating Pacific Front from far western Oklahoma into western-north Texas. A mix of supercells and a well-developed quasi-linear convective system (QLCS) yielded reports of large to very large hail and wind damage across portions of the area.
episodes.211762: An intensifying upper storm system instigated a period of severe thunderstorms across much of the WFO Norman Forecast area during the evening of the 1st. Storm development occurred both along a quasi-stationary boundary across northern Oklahoma and along an accelerating Pacific Front from far western Oklahoma into western-north Texas. A mix of supercells and a well-developed quasi-linear convective system (QLCS) yielded reports of large to very large hail and wind damage across portions of the area. A brief tornado was also documented in far eastern Wilbarger County in Texas.
episodes.211857: A band of slow moving storms, trained over the area producing flooding on several creeks and streams with rainfall amounts in excess of 3 to 5 inches.
episodes.211901: A band of slow moving storms, trained over the area producing flooding on several creeks and streams with rainfall amounts in excess of 3 to 5 inches.
episodes.211931: Strong to severe thunderstorms developed over central Oklahoma during the late afternoon of the 1st, along and ahead of an approaching cold front and associated strong upper level disturbance. The thunderstorms moved through portions of northeastern Oklahoma during the evening hours, the strongest of which produced large hail up to quarter size and damaging wind.
episodes.212005: During the afternoon and evening of April 2nd, 2026,  and early spring supercell thunderstorm event spread across eastern Iowa and northwest Illinois. This brought several swaths of damaging wind, large hail, and several tornadoes to both Iowa and Illinois.
episodes.212006: During the afternoon and evening of April 2nd, 2026,  and early spring supercell thunderstorm event spread across eastern Iowa and northwest Illinois. This brought several swaths of damaging wind, large hail, and several tornadoes to both Iowa and Illinois.
episodes.212144: A broken line of thunderstorms developed over Illinois in the afternoon and tracked into northern Indiana. Wind gusts of 55 mph to 65 mph were recorded resulting in at least one instance of tree and property damage.
episodes.212375: Low to mid level east-southeasterly flow and moderate instability favored sea breeze convection that produced a waterspout over the Caloosahatchee River near Whiskey Creek and a strong marine wind gust over Tampa Bay waters.
episodes.212443: Deep moisture in the lower troposphere combined with a trough of low pressure over Cuba resulted in vigorous convection over the eastern Straits of Florida, producing isolated gale force winds over the reef offshore the Upper Florida Keys.
episodes.212464: Low pressure and a warm front brought a round of severe thunderstorms to southern WI during the evening. Large hail and damaging straight-line winds occurred.
episodes.212777: A wet pattern developed during the first days of the month as above normal moisture, a nearby upper-level trough and a weak  trade wind cap supported shower and thunderstorm development. This included frequent passing showers across windward sectors, followed by enhanced afternoon convection. Flooding and Landslide reports where received during this period, April 1st to 5th.
episodes.213053: An upper-level trough moved across a dryline northwest of South-Central Texas and generated thunderstorms that moved into our area. Storm motion was toward the east-northeast while the low-level flow was from the southeast. This vertical wind shear in one of the storms was enough to produce a tornado.
episodes.213075: Scattered showers and storms developed ahead of a slow moving cold front on the evening of April 1, 2026.
episodes.213152: A few severe thunderstorms with damaging winds occurred across the Big Country.
episodes.213177: A complex storm system brought numerous severe thunderstorm winds to northern UT and a flash flooding event to the San Rafael Swell.
episodes.213194: A warm and moist airmass was in place across southeast Louisiana on April 2nd, with scattered to numerous thunderstorms developing during the afternoon and evening hours. Storms became oriented north to south and repeatedly redeveloped while slowly shifting east across Tangipahoa Parish. This allowed heavy rainfall to fall over some of the same areas for an extended period. A stronger storm also produced localized wind damage near Tickfaw.
episodes.213233: A mesoscale low with embedded thunderstorms tracked northeast across the Blue Mountain foothills, producing strong wind gusts across portions of Umatilla, OR and Walla Walla, WA counties the afternoon of the 1st.

The National Weather Service determined an EF-0 tornado touched down in Lee County this morning based on photos and drone footage received by the Lee County office of emergency management, combined with radar analysis. The tornado formed roughly six miles southwest of Giddings, roughly near the CR 208 and FM 2239, and moved northeast into Giddings before dissipating. Sporadic damage was observed to power lines, tree limbs, and tin sheds, as well as some small sections of tin roofs and eaves peeled back. Peak winds of 70 mph were estimated.

An EF-1 tornado began in far eastern Whiteside County just north of Fulfs Road and just west of the Whiteside-Lee county line, where satellite imagery showed the beginning of a narrow southwest-northeast path of disturbed soil through farm fields. Drone footage taken along Mound Hill Road in Lee County revealed swirl marks in the field to the west that aligned with the path that was evident in the satellite imagery, confirming that the tornado remained on the ground continuously as it tracked into Lee County. The tornado crossed Mound Hill Road, downing a number of power poles and impacting a property on the east side of the road. The tornado reached its peak intensity here, destroying multiple outbuildings and snapping several trees at this property. The tornado left additional swirl marks in a field to the northeast of the property before causing damage to trees, a residence, and a metal outbuilding along and just south of Lenox Road. As the tornado reached Timber Creek Road, it caused damage to a barn, at least one power pole, and several trees. On the north side of the road, the tornado pushed an old barn off of its foundation into a grain leg, causing the grain leg to collapse. A concrete silo was also toppled at the same location. The tornado then continued northeastward, causing tree and roof damage at a property along Peek Home Road, then damaging an outbuilding, a house, and more trees at a property at Penrose Road and Swarts Road. The tornado produced its last instance of damage at the Hey Tree Service facility along U.S. Route 52/State Route 26 southeast of Woosung before dissipating prior to reaching the Ogle County line. Straight-line wind damage was also observed to the south and east of the tornado's track.

It tracked for over 6.5 miles before lifting near the town of Woosung. A very brief EF-0 tornado dropped from locally lower ceilings within a bookend vortex embedded in the QLCS near Cecil Harden Lake, 1.3 miles southeast of the Hollandsburg community.  The bookend vortex crossed the lake, spawning the weak spin-up one-quarter mile south of the lake's southeastern shoreline;  along its 900-foot track, the tornado then crossed residential roads East Mallard Drive and South Ebert Drive, before ending 400 feet south of the lake's shore.||Drone imagery showed clear convergence of downed trees in a grove between Meadows Lane and Mallard Drive;  30 to 40 additional trees were either uprooted or snapped along the path.  Incident structural damage was limited to minor siding loss.  The tornado's damage was mainly vegetation, with peak ind gusts of 85 mph for the event.
